_about: How far the grand campaign's chart reaches. 'far' false: Europe and the Americas with their cities, as the cities version plays them. 'far' true: the whole world, with the Pacific and the globe laid after them (step 13 and the globe's stage) and the countries that live there. One line, flipped by the rules builder when the far side ships; until then nothing of the far side is read, so no campaign and no war moves. A test of the far side turns it on for its own file alone (src/campaign/stage.ts).
_convoyBattle: The wolf pack and convoy battle (release 2; Brian's yes of 20 November 2026, ruling 241 of 22 November). Off: nothing of the convoy battle runs, no extra die is thrown, and every war is the war of release 1. On: the grand campaigns opened from now on carry the flag 'convoyBattle' (set at a campaign's start only, never in one under way): every month on a convoy route takes a swing (data/campaign/convoybattle.json), and a night the player fights is booked back through navy.ts convoyField. A run outside the browser can be given it by TC_CONVOY=1.
_fortRows: The fortress rows (the design director's 05:38Z-06:21Z of 22 November 2026; data/campaign/fortrows.json): the book's fortress crews by date, taking no place among the five, their works holding all round, and beaten crews staying in their works as the town's garrison on their own stores. Off, the game is release 1's, war for war. A run outside the browser can force it: TC_FORTS=1 or TC_FORTS=0.
_yieldRule: The yield form (the design director's 05:30Z, 06:41Z and 07:20Z of 22 November 2026; data/campaign/capitulations.json; src/campaign/yield.ts): a beaten country yields when its field army is beaten and no ally's relief can reach it, and at stops 1-2 a computer-run country yields in the record's month after the first blow. A second way in beside the fall that release 1 has. Off, the game is release 1's, war for war. A run outside the browser can force it: TC_YIELD=1 or TC_YIELD=0.
_bargains: A neutral's bargains (release 2; Brian's yes of 22 November 2026, the design director's frame of 03:42 UTC and ruling of 03:47 UTC). Off: nothing of src/campaign/bargains.ts runs and every war is the war of release 1. On: the grand campaigns opened from now on carry the flag 'bargains', and their neutrals sell their goods to whichever country at war bids best (data/campaign/bargains.json). A test turns it on for its own games by setting that flag; a run outside the browser by TC_BARGAINS=1.
_legions: Volunteer legions (release 2; Brian's yes of 22 November 2026, the design director's frame of 03:42 UTC and rulings of 03:47 and 03:55 UTC). Off: nothing of src/campaign/legions.ts runs and every war is the war of release 1. On: the grand campaigns opened from now on carry the flag 'legions', and a country at peace outside both sides may send one legion of volunteers at a time to fight in a patron's army (data/campaign/legions.json). A test turns it on for its own games by setting that flag; a run outside the browser by TC_LEGIONS=1.
_winChance: The honest win chance on land (release 2; auto-resolve fix 1, Brian's yes of 23 November 2026 07:11Z and the design director's orders of 07:06Z, 07:27Z and 10:14Z; data/campaign/winchance.json). Its own step inside Units decide: it needs 'unitsDecide' too, and stays off, card and field both, until the 3D field's win share by odds band is within a tenth of the card's curve. Off: every battle throws today's luck and nothing changes. On: the grand campaigns opened from now on with Units decide carry the flag 'winChance' as well, and an attack in the field carries the ground at the record's rate for its odds (wider luck, losses unchanged). A test turns it on for its own games by setting both flags; a run outside the browser by TC_UNITS=1 TC_WINCHANCE=1.
_spread: The field spread (release 2; rules-builder/release2/field-spread/form.md, ruled by the design director 24 November 2026 19:47Z, 'Go ahead with step 1'; src/campaign/spread.ts, data/campaign/spread.json): one draw per battle, keyed on the field ticket's own seed and attempt. It holds the fortune share the field already fights on and one break point per side, the share of its power a side will lose before it quits, drawn about a level that comes from the side's own units (organisation, morale, experience, the general), never from a nation's flag or the date. Its own step inside Units decide: it needs 'unitsDecide' too, and is never on with 'winChance' (setSpread refuses the pair). Bench-only through the form's steps 1-4: nothing reads this key, no grand start offers it, and only a measuring harness sets the flag (setSpread) or lays the draw on its own tickets (spreadKeys). At step 5, if the six bands pass, card and field switch together. Off: no ticket carries reckoning.spread, no die is thrown on the campaign's dice or the field's, and every war and every field is the one without it.
_trueReach: True reach (audit item 41; the design director's ruling of 13:58Z, 'Withering garrisons' 1, and 14:26Z, 'Ports fed by an ally's paper reach', 25 November 2026): a sea the shutting power holds closed to the nation fed is closed to every ship carrying it stores, whatever the flag, so an ally's ships feed a port only where they could truly sail there with that nation's stores (game.ts trueReach). On wherever the far side is on. On the old chart its own step inside Units decide: it needs 'unitsDecide' too, and stays off, bench only, until its 96-war gate passes (Malta's and Tripoli's months in supply, Britain's corps lost there, how often each is besieged and taken, Italy's months to fall). Off: the supply picture is today's. On: the grand campaigns opened from now on with Units decide carry the flag 'trueReach' as well. A test turns it on by setTrueReach; a run outside the browser by TC_UNITS=1 TC_TRUEREACH=1.
_fromWait: The old chart's 'from' rows wait on contact (release 2; the design director's ruling of 19:47Z, 25 November 2026, pacific-japan/dd-form-from-rows-contact-1125.md; game.ts expeditions, drawn.ts corpsInContact). In the grand campaign a dated row that takes a named corps whole (its 'from' list, or the book's) waits while that corps stands in contact, an enemy at war on its province or beside it, and its half year runs from the month the corps comes free; where the corps already stands at the place the row forms, the row goes ahead. The far side has the same wait by its own rule. Off until its gate passes: the row takes the corps wherever it stands, as today, and every war is the war without it. On: the grand campaigns opened from now on carry the flag 'fromWait'. A run outside the browser can force it: TC_FROMWAIT=1 or TC_FROMWAIT=0.
_unitsDecide: Units decide (release 2; Brian 23 November 2026 07:11Z and 07:13Z, the core theme; the design director's audit of 07:17Z): battles come from the units each side built, researched and trained, never from a nation's flag or the date (src/campaign/units.ts). Off: nothing behind it is read and every war is the war without it. On: the grand campaigns opened from now on carry the flag 'unitsDecide' (set at a campaign's start only). Its steps so far: the convoy war by cause (data/campaign/convoycause.json). A run outside the browser can force it: TC_UNITS=1 or TC_UNITS=0.
_nicknames: Earned nicknames (release 2; Brian's yes of 23 November 2026 12:05Z; src/campaign/nicknames.ts, data/campaign/nicknames.json): a corps that wins several hard fights is given a name by its own army, in its nation's own style, and the name is shown on its flag. Every nation alike; a name changes no number. Off: nothing of it is read and every war is the war without it. On: the grand campaigns opened from now on carry the flag 'nicknames' (the player can also turn it on or off in a campaign under way: a name is only a name). A run outside the browser can force it: TC_NICKNAMES=1 or TC_NICKNAMES=0.
_columns: Supply columns (release 2; Brian's yes of 23 November 2026 12:05Z; src/campaign/columns.ts, data/campaign/columns.json): every month lorry columns drive from each nation's railhead along the roads to its corps beyond it, and enemy aircraft or partisans can ambush them on the way; what is lost never reaches the front. Outcomes come from what is on the ground and in the air (escorts, air cover, the partisans' strength), never from a nation or a date. Off: nothing of it is read and every war is the war without it. On: the grand campaigns opened from now on carry the flag 'columns' (set at a campaign's start only). A run outside the browser can force it: TC_COLUMNS=1 or TC_COLUMNS=0.
_logistics: Three supply orders on top of the supply columns (release 2; Brian's yes of 23 November 2026 13:06Z; src/campaign/logistics.ts, data/campaign/logistics.json), each its own switch and each read only where the columns run: 'lorryShift' (a nation's lorries are as many as its industry and fuel give, and go first to the front it names), 'wagons' (horse-drawn wagons carry what the lorries cannot, slower, and the ground tells on both) and 'dumps' (forward dumps stocked beyond the railhead feed the corps near them by a shorter road; bombing burns them and losing the ground loses them). Off: nothing of them is read. On: the grand campaigns opened from now on carry the flag (set at a campaign's start only). Forced by TC_LORRYSHIFT, TC_WAGONS, TC_DUMPS (1 or 0).
_fleetAttack: A fleet sent straight at an enemy fleet (release 2; Brian 23 November 2026 22:23Z: drag a fleet onto theirs and the battle is fought, as an army attacks; src/campaign/fleetattack.ts, data/campaign/fleetattack.json). The player's own order, in his month, at any odds, told them first, at sea or in the enemy's harbour. Off: nothing of it is read, no die is thrown and every war is the war without it. On: the grand campaigns opened from now on carry the flag 'fleetAttack' (the player can also turn it on or off in a campaign under way). A run outside the browser can force it: TC_FLEETATTACK=1 or TC_FLEETATTACK=0.
_breakUp: Breaking a corps up (release 2; Brian 24 November 2026 18:02Z: "when I click on a unit stack, I want to be able to see each individual unit apart of it. that way i can break it up if needed"; src/campaign/breakup.ts, data/campaign/breakup.json). The player picks divisions of one of his corps and splits them off as a corps of their own where it stands; a part rejoins the corps it came from. Off: nothing of it is read and every war is the war without it. On: the grand campaigns opened from now on carry the flag 'breakUp' (the player can also turn it on or off in a campaign under way). A run outside the browser can force it: TC_BREAKUP=1 or TC_BREAKUP=0.
_marked: The marked army (release 2; Brian 24 November 2026 18:01Z, 'yes to all', the third idea of the enemy's month near you; src/campaign/marked.ts): the enemy corps that takes one of the player's towns wears a red tag on the table, and its card says what it took, until he beats it; beating it, or its end, clears the mark with a line of news. No more than three at once. A mark changes no number. Off: nothing of it is read and every war is the war without it. On: the grand campaigns opened from now on carry the flag 'marked' (the player can also turn it on or off in a campaign under way). A run outside the browser can force it: TC_MARKED=1 or TC_MARKED=0.
_taskForce: Task forces (release 2; Brian 24 November 2026 18:24Z, 'i like these'; src/campaign/taskforce.ts, data/campaign/taskforce.json). One of the player's fleets at sea on a job is made a task force: each month it comes in to refit when worn and goes back to its job when fit, until he changes it. Off: nothing of it is read. On: the grand campaigns opened from now on carry the flag 'taskForce' (the player can also turn it on or off in a campaign under way). A run outside the browser can force it: TC_TASKFORCE=1 or TC_TASKFORCE=0.
_fleetWhy: The admirals' reasons (release 2; Brian 24 November 2026 18:32Z, 'the navy needs a lot of work and attention', and the plan sent to him: 'the admirals don't explain themselves'; src/campaign/fleetwhy.ts). Where the player's admirals run the navy for him, each fleet they order carries one sentence saying why it is where it is, on its page and its panel. It changes nothing in the war. Off: nothing is written. On: the grand campaigns opened from now on carry the flag 'fleetWhy' (the player can also turn it on or off in a campaign under way). A run outside the browser can force it: TC_FLEETWHY=1 or TC_FLEETWHY=0.
_rearguard: Rearguards (release 2; Brian 24 November 2026 18:24Z, 'i like these', of the idea 'a split-off division can hold a province for a month while your main army pulls back, slowing the enemy's pursuit'; src/campaign/rearguard.ts, data/campaign/rearguard.json). A small corps of the player's is ordered to hold where it stands until his next month; an enemy army that attacks it loses weeks of its month, and under Units decide it screens the corps falling back behind it from the pursuit. Off: nothing of it is read. On: the grand campaigns opened from now on carry the flag 'rearguard' (the player can also turn it on or off in a campaign under way). A run outside the browser can force it: TC_REARGUARD=1 or TC_REARGUARD=0.
_settledTowns: Conquered towns settle (release 2; Brian 24 November 2026 18:12Z and 18:13Z: every kind of building in a conquered city, after a short wait; src/campaign/buildings.ts, data/campaign/buildings.json 'settle'). A town taken from another country can put up every line of building and the military works once it has been held a few months, and its buildings then serve its holder as at home. One rule for every country. Off: nothing of it is read and every war is the war without it. On: the grand campaigns opened from now on carry the flag 'settledTowns' (the player can also turn it on or off in a campaign under way). A run outside the browser can force it: TC_SETTLEDTOWNS=1 or TC_SETTLEDTOWNS=0.
_shadow: Shadowing (release 2; Brian 24 November 2026 19:47Z, 'yes to all'; src/campaign/shadow.ts, data/campaign/shadow.json). A fleet of cruisers set on an enemy fleet follows it month by month while it is in reach, keeps it identified for its side, and reports where it is; it seeks no battle and mostly keeps its distance when found alone. The computer's admirals set shadows by the same rule. Off: no fleet carries a shadow and every war is the war without it. On: the grand campaigns opened from now on carry the flag 'shadow' (the player can also turn it on or off in a campaign under way). Forced by TC_SHADOW=1 or 0.
_voyageLog: The voyage log (release 2; Brian 24 November 2026 19:47Z, 'yes to all'; src/campaign/voyage.ts, data/campaign/voyage.json). Each fleet writes where it was and what it fought at every month's end, shown on its page. A record only: no rule reads it. Off: nothing is written or shown. On: the grand campaigns opened from now on carry the flag 'voyageLog' (switchable in any month). Forced by TC_VOYAGELOG=1 or 0.
_rearBridges: Rearguards blow the bridges (release 2; Brian 24 November 2026 19:47Z, 'yes to all'; src/campaign/rearguard.ts rearBridgesOn, rivers.ts bridgesOnCapture, data/campaign/rearguard.json 'bridges'). Read only with rearguards on: a province a rearguard held is lost, and the bridges behind it go up on the rearguard's laid charges instead of the usual chance. Off: the usual chance, as for any province. On: the grand campaigns opened from now on carry the flag 'rearBridges' (switchable in any month). Forced by TC_REARBRIDGES=1 or 0.
_seaMines: Mines at sea (release 2; Brian 24 November 2026 20:38Z, 'yes to all'; src/campaign/mines.ts, data/campaign/mines.json). A fleet with destroyers, cruisers or submarines lays a field across a narrow sea or off an enemy fleet's harbour; enemy ships sailing there may lose a ship each month until destroyers sweep it. The computer's admirals lay fields too. Switchable in any month from OPTIONS.
_heavySeas: Heavy seas (release 2; Brian 24 November 2026 20:38Z, 'yes to all'; src/campaign/heavyseas.ts, data/campaign/heavyseas.json). Gales blow under a closed sky at sea, mostly in winter: ships can sail into a sea in a gale but not on through it that month, convoys through one are late, and a shadow may lose its quarry in one. The same for every country. Switchable in any month from OPTIONS.
_shadowRelay: The shadow relay (release 2; Brian 24 November 2026 20:38Z, 'yes to all'; src/campaign/shadow.ts, data/campaign/shadow.json 'relay'). Read only with shadowing on: a shadow's fuel lasts three months on station, and then a fresh cruiser fleet from harbour takes over without losing contact. Switchable in any month from OPTIONS.
_seekOnce: A fleet seeks battle once a month (release 2; the design director's ruling of 25 November 2026, 02:38Z, on the navy thread's finding that a fleet could seek more than once: in every allied nation's month-end meeting, and at month's end after an order of attack that missed or struck a harbour; src/campaign/navy.ts). Each fleet on the seeking side of a fleet action, by the player's order or in any nation's month-end meeting, the player's and the computer's alike, is marked with the month; a marked fleet is left out of every later meeting that month and cannot be sent at the enemy again. An order of attack counts whether it finds its quarry or misses. Defenders are never marked: a fleet that fought can still be found and fought. Off: nothing is marked and every war is the war without it.
_townQueue: A queue for a town (release 2; Brian 25 November 2026 13:41Z, 'easy to manage the cities, recruitment, ect'; the design director's ruling seamless-r2-1125.md part B; src/campaign/townqueue.ts). The player lines up what each of his towns builds next; each queued building is a press of BUILD made for him at the opening of his month, straight after his staff's month, at that day's price and through BUILD's own checks. One the treasury cannot pay for waits at the head of its town's queue; one refused for any other reason comes off with a line saying why; a lost town's queue goes, unpaid. The staff never touches it. Off: nothing of it is read or written and every war is the war without it. On: the grand campaigns opened from now on carry the flag 'townQueue' (switchable in any month from OPTIONS). Forced by TC_TOWNQUEUE=1 or 0.
_atomBomb: The atomic project (release 2; Brian 25 November 2026 01:14Z, 'lets do number 1'; the design director's ruling of 01:27Z; src/campaign/atom.ts, data/campaign/atom.json). Three rows of the Industry branch, then atomic plants that draw a share of a nation's earnings every month for years toward one fixed bill: a large industry finishes them, a small one never. Then a bomb or two, carried by an ordinary bombing raid on an enemy city that is not a capital: the city in ruins and a weight on that country's will to fight through the surrender rules. Spies, bombing and capture set the plants back. The same rules for every country; the book's stops hold the computer to the record's clock. Off: the rows leave the tree and nothing is drawn. On: the grand campaigns opened from now on carry the flag 'atom' (switchable in any month from OPTIONS). Forced by TC_ATOM=1 or 0.
_carrierStrike: Carrier strikes on harbours by the player's own hand (release 2; Brian 24 November 2026 21:45Z, 'Resume the Pacific for release 2', and the 19 November Pacific playtest's first finding: a player who runs his navy himself had no order to gather a striking force and fly it, and nothing told him why a strike did not fly; src/campaign/harbourstrike.ts). A carrier fleet's page lists the enemy harbours with warships at anchor that its strike aircraft can reach from a sea in its reach, and one order sails it there and sends its wings in. A harbour beyond them names a base from which they reach it; a harbour of a country at peace says to declare war first. The player's order only: no staff reads it, so every computer war is the war without it.
_wingByDate: Carrier wings by date (release 2; the design director's riders of 17 November 2026 to rulings 189 and 202, built by the navy thread 25 November 2026 on the far side's audit; src/campaign/carriers.ts, carriers.json 'wingByDate'). A navy's wing a deck changes on the dates its row gives: Britain's from 12 fighters and 24 strike aircraft to 24 and 12 in August 1942, 28 and 20 in January 1944 and 37 and 17 in January 1945, on every British carrier, Europe's too. Room taken away sends what is over to the reserve; room added fills as losses are made good, in harbour: nothing is given. A player who is Britain is told in the month's news. Off: every navy's wing stands as it was for the whole war.
_ferry: Moving an air group to any airfield of its side's or its allies' with one order (release 2; Brian 24 November 2026 22:08Z; src/campaign/ferry.ts, data/campaign/ferry.json). The group flies by a chain of friendly fields within its ferry range, a few hops a month, out of the fight on the way, and the order says how many turns it takes and whether enemy fighters are known within reach of the way; where no chain reaches across an ocean it goes crated by sea. The computer's staffs use it for their spare groups. Off, nothing of it runs and no die is drawn. A run outside the browser can be given it by TC_FERRY=1.
_airNames: Better air unit names (release 2; Brian 25 November 2026: 'can we come up with better names for the airforce squadrons?'; the design director's ruling of 03:18Z, design-director/air-names-1125.md; src/campaign/air.ts groupName, data/campaign/air-names.json '_airNames'). Words only: on, a new air group is named with the numbers its arm really used, the role in the name only where the arm put it there (else shown beside the name), in its arm's own plain form where no rung is near, and Japan's island groups by their airfield. (Italy's day-one names were dropped by Brian's answer of 03:31Z; its words are its earned list, under 'nicknames'.) Off: every name as ruling 220 gives it. A group keeps the name it was given for life, whatever the switch says later, and a saved war keeps its names. The grand campaigns opened while this is true carry the flag 'airNames'; it can be switched in any month from OPTIONS (new groups only). A run outside the browser can force it: TC_AIRNAMES=1 or TC_AIRNAMES=0.
_offers: Formations offered (release 2, Japan and the Pacific; the design director's ruling B8 of 25 November 2026 and his 13:39Z of that day: 'B8 stays OFF until its screen is built and passes the Mac. Then ON under Brian's 01:10Z rule'; src/campaign/game.ts offersOn, unreal/TheaterCommand/Rules/offers-look.ts). Read only on the whole world (the far switch). On: a dated row that would take corps of the player's own off the map is an offer on the month's one list, never a silent removal; so is the end of a loan whose division awaits the regiment, and a reorganisation of his own forces (Oahu's split); an offer lapses by the one lapse rule, and the 3D game has its page FORMATIONS OFFERED and a row on the month card. Off: no offer is ever made, no flag of it is written or read, there is no page and no row, and the player's dated rows come and go as a computer's do. A computer's rows are the same either way, so no war nobody plays moves. The grand campaigns opened while this is true carry the flag 'offers' (set at a campaign's start only). A run outside the browser can force it: TC_OFFERS=1 or TC_OFFERS=0.
